div.l: And all the remenant of oure pilgrimage
But first I pray you of your curtesie
That ye rette it nat to my vilenie
Thouȝ that I pleinli speke in this mater
To telle you of the wordes ⁊and of the cheer
Ne thouȝ I speke her wordes propirly
For this ye knowe as wel as I
Who so telle a tale aftir a man̄
He must reherse as ny as euer he can
Eueri word of it be in his charge
Thouȝ he speke neuer so rudeli ne so large
Orellis he must telle his tale vntrewe
Or fein thing or fynde wordes newe
He may nouȝt spare al thouȝ he were his brothir
He must aswell say oo word as an othir
Crist spak him self full brode in holi writ
And well ye wott no vilenie is it
Eke Plato seith who so can him rede
The worde must be cosin to the dede
Also I pray you to foryeue it me
All haue I not sett hou in here degre
Hiere in this tale as I shuld stonde
My witt is short ye shal wel vnderstande
Gret chiere made oure oost vs euerichon̄
And to the souper set he vs anon
He serued vs with vitaill ate beste
Straunge was the wyn̄ and wel to drink vs leste
A semeli man was oure oost with all
For to be a Marshall in a lordes hall
A large man he was with yhen stepe
A fairer burgeis ther is non in chepe
Bolde of his speking and wise ⁊and wel I tauȝt
And of manhod he wanted right nouȝt
Eke therto he was a mery man
And aftirsouper pleyen he began̄
And spak of mirthe among othir thinges
Whan that we had made oure rekenynges
He seid thus now Lordinges truly
Ye be to me riȝt welcome hertely
For be my trouthe if I shuld nat lye
I saugh nat this yere somery acompanie
Atones in herberugh as is now
Fain wold I don to you mirthe ⁊and I wist hou
And of a mirthe I am right now be thouȝt
To don̄ you ease and it shal cost you nouȝt
Ye gon to Caunterbury god you spede
The blisfull martir quite you your mede
And wel I wot as ye gon by the wey
Ye shape to tale and to pley
For truli confort nor mirthe is ther non̄
To ride by the weie as dombe as a ston
And therfor wold I make disport
As I said erst to don you som comfort
And if ye liken alle of oon assent
For to stonden at my Iugement
And for to werchen as I shal you say
To morwe whan ye riden by the way
Now be my faders soule that is ded
But yef ye be mery I will yeue you myn̄ hed
Holde vp your handes withouten more speche
Oure counseill was nat longe for to seche
Vs thouȝt it was nat worth to make it uice
And graunted him withoute more avys
And bad him sey his verdit as him list
Now Lordinges quod he herkeneth for the best
And take it nouȝt I pray you in disdein
This is the point to speke it short and plein
That ich of you to shorte with your weie
In this viage shall telle tales tweye
To Caunterbury ward I ment so
And homward he shal telle othir tuo
Of Auentures that whilom han befalle
And wich of you that bereth him best of alle
That is to seyn that tellith in this cas
Tales of best sentence and most solas
Shall haue a souper all of oure alderes cost
Hiere in this place sitting by this post
Whan that we comen̄ ayen from Caunterbury
And for to make you the more mery
I will my self with you gladly ride
Riȝt at myn ougne cost and be your guide
And so that my Iugement with seye
Shall pay al that we shal spende by the weye
And if ye vouchesaf that it be so
Telle me anon̄ withouten̄ wordes mo
And I will erli shape me therfore
This thing was graunted and oure othes swore
With full glad herte and praien him also
